interface.title: Hydro Lens — Portable Optical Microplastic Screening (legacy Streamlit fallback app, app.py)
interface.field: Environmental science / water quality (microplastics in filtered water samples, optical microscopy)
interface.stage_of_work: Field screening and lab triage: image analysis of filtered samples before confirming them by FTIR/Raman
interface.what_it_is_for: Detects and sizes candidate microplastic particles in a microscope image of a water filter using a calibrated µm/pixel factor, then gives a sample confidence score, per-particle lab-confirmation flags, a size histogram, a particles-per-litre estimate and a JSON report.

data.note: Scope: according to the reviewer's reading of README.md, the primary Hydro Lens UI is React + FastAPI and app.py is the legacy Streamlit fallback demo. This tree covers only the Streamlit app. I used the three bundled demo images (Demo Microplastics Sample (Mixed Candidates), Blank Filter Control, Stage Micrometer Scale). I also uploaded the test files demo_microplastic_sample.jpg to Analyze Sample and stage_micrometer_scale.png to the calibration wizard. The YOLOv8n model failed to load ('operator torchvision::nms does not exist'), so every detection came from the heuristic OpenCV fallback ('Operating in Demo/Heuristic mode'). On the mixed sample it detected 300 tiny noise 'fragments' and missed the obvious shapes (screens/010.webp). The bundled calibration started as STALE (0.417 µm/px, expired 2026-10-03), not VALID as the notes expected. My calibration runs overwrote the app's saved calibration: it is now 0.4167 µm/px, valid until 2026-11-06.

features.name: Calibration status gate with expiry badge
features.general: Keep the active instrument calibration in a persistent badge and banner that shows its state (valid, stale, or missing/invalid), its factor and its expiry, and warn or down-weight measurements when it is not valid
features.specific: Sidebar 📊 Calibration Status badge (VALID & ACTIVE / STALE (> 7 Days) / MISSING / INVALID) plus the Analyze Sample banner ('Results will be marked with a 0.5 quality factor'), driven by calibration.json timestamp/expires/valid
steps: Open any page and read the badge and factor
Read the banner on the analysis page
Return and see the badge change state
serves_tasks: Check whether the current scale factor can be trusted

features.note: Observed issues: the sidebar badge updated only after navigating away from the wizard. A run under STALE calibration raised no calibration flag in the flags list. Blocking of output under MISSING/INVALID calibration was not observed.

features.name: Two-step scale calibration wizard (compute, then validate and save)
features.general: Compute a pixel-to-length factor from a reference ruler image, either automatically or from a hand-measured distance, then check it against reference objects of known size and save it with pass/fail per reference and an expiry date
features.specific: Calibration Portal → Step 1: Method A FFT line detection on an uploaded or preset stage micrometer image, or Method B 'Measured Distance in Pixels' ÷ 'Number of Scale Divisions (10µm each)'; Step 2: Magnification and Camera fields plus measured 10/50/100 µm bead sizes → Save & Activate Calibration (per-bead error_pct, PASS/FAIL, valid flag, 7-day expiry)
steps: Upload a micrometer image or tick the preset
Press Calculate via FFT, or enter pixel distance and number of divisions and press Set Factor Manually
Open Step 2 and enter the measured bead sizes
Read the saved JSON (per-bead PASS/FAIL, valid)
serves_tasks: Compute a scale factor from a reference ruler image
Validate the scale against reference objects of known size and save it
features.note: Method A (FFT) failed on both the preset and the uploaded stage micrometer image ('Could not automatically detect stage micrometer lines'); only Method B produced a factor.
